narrative.overview:
Halo's components are panes of coated glass hung in a bright gallery, and their motion shows up as moving light. The room is a cool-white wall with graphite ink and hairline steel wires; the only colour in it is the cyan, magenta, and amber coating on a pane's edge and the soft pools of light that pane throws on the wall. Docs read like wall text and museum object labels: a large display headline, a quiet lede, and a small label that lists title, date, medium, and dimensions, where the dimensions are the API.

The system runs as two worlds sharing one structure, switched live through `data-world` on the root: **Dichroic** (default) and **Partition**, the same room behind acid-etched glass with aluminium mullions dividing the page into bays, no hue, and silhouette shadows instead of coloured light. Each world has a light and a dark theme through `data-theme`. Page structure, type, spacing, and components never change between worlds; only tokens do.

Density is gallery-sparse: one idea per section, generous section padding, a left column of wall text and a right column of working material. Everything that moves is driven by the library's own spring solver, so the site is itself the demo. The page refuses the dark neon dev-tool landing page and the centred headline over a row of cards, and it must look nothing like Anthropic or Claude UI.
keyCharacteristics: Cool-white gallery wall (never cream) with graphite ink; ink, not a hue, is the accent.
Coat colours exist only on pane edges and in the light the panes cast.
One material, `.halo-surface`: frosted pane, padding-box edge ring, layered shadow.
Two runtime worlds (Dichroic, Partition) times two themes, all from tokens on one DOM.
Motion from the spring solver only; CSS transitions borrow a curve sampled from it.
Pills for every control, hairlines for every division, no card grids.

rules.name: The Edge-and-Light Rule
rules.body: Coat hues live on a pane's edge ring and in the light it casts, plus the text selection tint and caret. They never fill a button, colour text, or tint a surface.

rules.name: The Ink Accent Rule
rules.body: The strongest emphasis on any screen is graphite ink on wall (or its inverse in dark). There is no brand hue to reach for.

rules.name: The Silent Partition Rule
rules.body: In Partition every coat token resolves to a neutral grey; the only chroma left on the page is the status icon colour.

rules.name: The Wall Text Rule
rules.body: Headings use the display face at weight 600 with negative tracking that grows with size (-0.015em at title, -0.03em at headline, -0.035em at display). Body copy is never set in the display face.

rules.name: The Object Label Rule
rules.body: Component specs are written as a museum label: title and date, italic medium, then a two-column list of dimensions (import, weight, peers, motion, accessibility) in 13px with faint terms and ink values.

rules.name: The Glass-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it is not a pane, it does not cast a shadow. Wall-level containers use an inset hairline ring (`inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line)`) instead.

rules.name: The Cast Light Rule
rules.body: Cast light is pure geometry: blurred ellipses moved by transform on a softer spring that trails the pane, blended with multiply (light) or screen (dark). It is never baked into an image.

rules.name: The Padding-Box Ring Rule
rules.body: The edge ring is masked padding-box against border-box, never content-box. A content-box mask leaves the ring thick and lumpy in the corners whenever the pane has padding; that bug shipped once and was caught by eye.

rules.name: The Pill Control Rule
rules.body: Anything you press is a pill. Anything that holds content is a rounded rectangle. Nothing on the wall has square corners except table rules and section borders.

dos: Do keep coat colour on pane edges and cast light only; reach for graphite ink when something needs emphasis.
Do build every new glass element from `.halo .halo-surface` so it inherits the blur, shadow, edge ring, and both worlds for free.
Do mask edge rings padding-box against border-box so the ring is one even width through the corners.
Do drive new motion from the spring solver, and use `--ease-spring` when it has to be CSS-only.
Do express world and theme differences as token overrides under `[data-world]` and `[data-theme]`, never as separate markup.
Do separate wall-level containers with tone and 1px inset hairline rings, not shadows.
Do write specs as object labels (title, medium, dimensions) and lists of options as hairline-ruled rows.
Do keep the time-left indicator opt-in, on the bottom edge, at edge-ring width.
Do provide the solid surface fallback for reduced transparency, higher contrast, and missing `backdrop-filter`.
donts: Don't use cream or warm off-white walls; the gallery is cool white (hue 250).
Don't colour buttons, text, or backgrounds with the coat hues.
Don't mask the edge ring against the content box.
Don't add shadows to wall-level cards, wells, or panels.
Don't animate height, width, or layout properties; transform and opacity only.
Don't use fixed-duration easing for anything that moves in response to a gesture.
Don't lay out a centred headline over a row of cards, or a dark neon dev-tool hero.
Don't introduce hue into Partition beyond status icons.
Don't borrow Anthropic or Claude UI styling.
